subject: model
value: The full pdftotext extraction for exactly one catalogued document.
justification: doc_id is declared PRIMARY KEY and is simultaneously a cascading foreign key to documents(id), which is the classic one-to-zero-or-one extension table: one row is the extracted body of one document. The only open subject is uniqueness of text. That is accidental. Nothing in the schema forbids two documents extracting to the same string, and the author explicitly anticipates byte-identical files through duplicate_sets(sha256, count, paths_json) - two paths holding the same PDF would yield identical text and immediately break text as a key. text is also the payload, never the identifier; the FTS mirror (document_fts(path, title, text)) treats it the same way. Scope is current-state for the same reason as documents: the row holds what pdftotext produced from the file now sitting at documents.path, and re-extraction after the file changes replaces it. atomicity_candidates is empty; had text been offered, it is one archived document body, i.e. atomic despite its length.

subject: author
justification: `author` is a concatenated free-text name-list, not an identifier: the same people appear under two different spellings in the sibling corpus of the same authority ('Kestutis Karciauskas, Jorg Peters' vs 'Kęstutis Karčiauskas, Jörg Peters'), so the string does not even identify the author group consistently. None of the listed attributes are owned. (a) author->topic is pure sparsity here — 10 distinct author strings over 12 rows, 8 distinct topics; in the sibling SurfLab catalog it holds only vacuously because `topic` has exactly 1 distinct value across all 43 rows. `topic` is a curatorial theme assigned by the corpus ranking lens, owned by the document, not by whoever wrote it. (b) author->original_author is the near-constant artifact: `original_author` is empty in 10 of 12 rows here and 28 of 43 in the sibling, so almost any column determines it. (c) author->inferred_author does hold stably — author and inferred_author are byte-identical in all 55 rows across both corpora — but that is a duplicated column produced by the provenance pipeline copying inferred_author into author, not an entity owning an attribute. The remediation is dropping the copy, not extracting an author entity. Since the judged `owns` set includes original_author and topic, both of which

subject: inferred_author
justification: Mirror image of the `author` candidate, and accidental for the same reasons. inferred_author is byte-identical to author in all 12 rows here and all 43 rows of the sibling SurfLab catalog, so the two columns are interchangeable and the observed FD is column duplication rather than ownership. inferred_author->original_author rides on original_author being empty in 10 of 12 rows. inferred_author->topic is sparsity: near-unique free-text determinant over a 12-row relation, and vacuous in the sibling where topic is constant at a single value. A free-text author string is not the entity that owns a corpus topic.

subject: original_title
justification: Doubly degenerate. `original_title` is a near-unique free-text column (empty in 4 of 12 rows, otherwise distinct, including junk PDF-metadata values like 'pnasSI201316348 1..9' and 'untitled'), and the target `original_author` is near-constant (empty in 10 of 12 rows; 28 of 43 in the sibling). The dependency holds because the determinant rarely repeats and the target rarely varies — it measures nothing about the domain. A title does not own an author; the document (identified by path/id) owns both.

subject: original_title,publication_year
justification: A composite of a near-unique free-text column with a near-unique bookkeeping integer (10 distinct years over 12 rows), determining `producer` — a PDF toolchain string ('pdfTeX-1.40.17', 'pikepdf 8.15.1', 'Acrobat Distiller 10.1.8 (Windows)') that is file metadata belonging to the byte stream, keyed by path/sha256. The composite is already nearly a key by chance, so it determines everything. Empirically refuted against the sibling corpus of the same authority and schema: 2 violating groups there.

subject: producer
justification: `producer` is the PDF-generator tool string; it has no relationship to authorship. It holds here only because 'pdfTeX-1.40.17' happens to cover rows 7, 8, 9, all of which have the empty `original_author` shared by 10 of 12 rows. Refuted directly in the sibling SurfLab catalog: 5 producer values map to more than one original_author.

subject: producer,publication_year
justification: Textbook composite of unrelated bookkeeping columns — a generator-tool string and a year — determining a free-text title. It survives here only because publication_year is nearly a key on its own (10 distinct values over 12 rows). Refuted in the sibling corpus: 3 violating (producer, publication_year) groups. A typesetting tool plus a year owns nothing.

subject: publication_year
justification: The clearest sparsity artifact in the packet: 10 distinct years over 12 rows, so publication_year is nearly a key by chance, and the target `original_author` is empty in 10 of 12 rows. The only repeated years (2014, 2019) happen to pair rows that both have the empty value. A year cannot own an author. Refuted in the sibling corpus: 7 violating year groups.

subject: publication_year,topic
justification: Composite of a near-key integer with a categorical label. Categories and years do not identify anything; this pair simply fails to collide in 12 rows. The one collision, (2014, tpms-gyroid), is a paper and its own supporting-information PDF, which trivially share an author list. Refuted decisively in the sibling corpus: 8 violating (publication_year, topic) groups.

subject: venue
justification: 11 distinct venue strings over 12 rows — a near-key by chance. The only repeat is 'Acta Cryst A' (rows 1 and 5), which agrees on both targets. Neither target is owned: `original_author` is the near-constant empty column (10 of 12 rows), and venue->producer is visibly false in the world even inside this table — the arXiv rows carry pdfTeX-1.40.17, pdfTeX-1.40.21 and pikepdf 8.15.1, colliding only because the venue strings were written at subject-class granularity ('arXiv (math.DG)', 'arXiv (cond-mat.soft)'). Sibling corpus shows a venue->original_author violation as well. A publication venue does not own a PDF generator string.

subject: model
value: One PDF file present in the corpus directory, together with its extracted metadata and the agent-authored bibliographic review of that file.
justification: The DDL declares exactly two identifying constraints: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE. Both are coherent, and one row is one file at one corpus-relative path. The 31 other observed UCCs are 12-row noise: title, filename, size_bytes, text_chars, creation_date, text_path, standard_filename, suggested_name, what_it_does, and every pair such as pages,topic or author,venue are descriptive attributes with no unique index and obvious collision potential in a larger corpus. sha256 deserves special mention because it looks key-like: the author refutes it in schema by creating duplicate_sets (sha256 TEXT PRIMARY KEY, count INTEGER, paths_json TEXT), a table whose only purpose is to record one hash occurring at several paths, and by indexing documents_sha256_idx non-uniquely. Scope is current-state, not invariant: path, sha256, size_bytes, pages, text_chars and the pdfinfo_* columns describe the file that sits at that path right now, so path -> sha256 holds of the snapshot and would break if a PDF were replaced in place. atomicity_candidates is empty; author is a delimited author list but was not put to me.
